summary: Intentionally consumes CPU time to simulate slower machines or stress-test frame-rate and cooking behavior.
key_concepts: Intentionally consumes CPU cycles to simulate slower machines or reduce a network's effective frame rate.
Active toggles whether the CPU delay is applied.
Cook Every Frame forces the operator to cook every frame, making the delay visible even without downstream demand.
Delay and Delay Unit define the minimum amount of time the CHOP wastes.
Use Info CHOP or operator info to monitor cook time, warnings, and errors when stress testing with Hog CHOP.
common_gotchas: Hog CHOP is deliberately expensive and should not be placed in generated production networks unless the task is performance simulation.
Cook Every Frame can degrade the entire project frame rate.
Delay settings should be kept small and explicit during tests.
This operator is useful for stress testing, not for real signal processing.
Generated plans should warn users before enabling it in live show files.
